AL.headline: Current Use valuation available; beekeeping not explicitly listed

requirements.minAcreage: No state minimum, varies by county

AL.notes: Alabama's Current Use program (Ala. Code § 40-7-25.1) values agricultural land at use value. Focuses on traditional farming, timber, and pasture. Apiculture not explicitly mentioned but may qualify as 'agricultural production' - check with county assessor.

AK.headline: No statewide agricultural use valuation program
AK.notes: Alaska has no statewide property tax. Boroughs (counties) set their own rules. Some boroughs may offer agricultural exemptions but no uniform statewide program exists. Limited commercial beekeeping due to climate.

AZ.headline: Agricultural classification available; beekeeping can qualify
AZ.notes: Arizona uses Class 3 agricultural classification (A.R.S. § 42-12001). Beekeeping can qualify as agricultural production. County assessor determines eligibility. Must demonstrate commercial agricultural operation.

CO.headline: Agricultural land classification with explicit beekeeping provisions

requirements.minAcreage: No minimum if income threshold met

CO.notes: Colorado allows agricultural classification for land used for 'apiculture' (C.R.S. § 39-1-102). Must generate $1,000+ income from agricultural products. One of the clearer states for beekeeping qualification.

CT.headline: PA 490 program explicitly includes beekeeping
CT.notes: Connecticut's PA 490 (Public Act 490) explicitly lists 'the keeping of bees' as a qualifying agricultural use. Very bee-friendly state for tax purposes. Apply through local assessor.

DE.headline: Agricultural use assessment exists; beekeeping status unclear
DE.notes: Delaware offers agricultural use valuation but beekeeping is not explicitly addressed in statutes. Traditional farming and timber are primary focus. Contact county assessment office for interpretation.

HI.headline: Agricultural dedication program; beekeeping qualifies
HI.notes: Hawaii's agricultural land dedication program (HRS Chapter 205) recognizes beekeeping. Strong honey industry due to climate. Each county administers differently. Agricultural use dedication provides significant tax reduction.

ID.headline: Agricultural exemption available; beekeeping qualifies
ID.notes: Idaho provides agricultural property tax exemption for land in agricultural use (Idaho Code § 63-604). Beekeeping operations can qualify as agricultural production. Must be operated commercially, not as hobby.

IL.headline: Farmland assessment with specific beekeeping provisions
IL.notes: Illinois farmland assessment (35 ILCS 200/10-110) explicitly includes 'apiculture' as agricultural use. Land must be 10+ acres or contiguous to farmland. Well-defined beekeeping provision.

IN.headline: Agricultural land base rate applies; beekeeping not explicitly listed
IN.notes: Indiana uses agricultural land base rate value (IC 6-1.1-4-13). Focuses on soil productivity for cropland. Beekeeping not explicitly addressed - may qualify if land otherwise qualifies for agricultural assessment. Check with county assessor.
